chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left behind a slave boy, and some of the heirs testified that he was free. He said: 'His testimony is accepted in his share, and the slave boy is compensated for what belonged to the others among the heirs.'
ai.seo_question: How is the testimony of heirs regarding a slave's manumission handled in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-ghurm bi al-ghunm* (liability corresponds to benefit) in inheritance disputes, where the testifying heirs bear the cost of their claim only to the extent of their own shares. It highlights the Shia juristic approach to balancing evidentiary weight with equitable compensation, ensuring the freed slave is not deprived of his status due to the partial testimony of specific heirs. This ruling underscores the precision of Shia fiqh in handling mixed-evidence scenarios within the broader context of *bayyinah* (proofs).
